question.text: The foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point (1,8,4) on the line joining the point (0,-11,4) and (2,-3,1) is

solution.text: Equation of line joining points (0,-11,4) and (2,-3,1) is $$ \frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y+3}{8}=\frac{z-1}{-3}=\lambda $$ Let $P$ is any point of the above line then coordinate of $P$ is $(2 \lambda+2,8 \lambda-3,-3 \lambda+1)$ $\therefore \mathrm{DR}^{\prime} \mathrm{s}$ of $P Q$ is $(2 \lambda+1,8 \lambda-11,-3 \lambda-3$ Now, $(2 \lambda+1)(4+(8 \lambda-11)(8)+(-3 \lambda-3) (-3)=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad 4 \lambda+2+64 \lambda-88+9 \lambda+9=0$ $77 \lambda-77=0$ $\therefore$ Required foot of perpendicular. $$ P(4,5,-2) $$
